slides.title: Plate tectonics: the unifying theory of geology
slides.body:
**Plate tectonics**: Earth's lithosphere (rigid outer ~100 km) is broken into ~15 major plates that move over the underlying asthenosphere (ductile mantle). Driving force: mantle convection + slab pull + ridge push.

Proposed by Alfred Wegener (continental drift, 1912) as 'Pangaea'. Initially rejected — no mechanism. Revived 1960s-70s with seafloor-spreading + paleomagnetism + seismology evidence. Now the unifying theory of geology.

**Evidence**:
- **Continental fit**: South America + Africa fit like jigsaw pieces.
- **Fossil distribution**: identical Mesosaurus + Glossopteris on now-separated continents.
- **Paleoclimate**: glacial deposits in tropical Africa, coal in Antarctica → continents were elsewhere.
- **Paleomagnetism**: magnetic minerals in rocks record Earth's field direction at time of cooling. Tracks show continents have moved.
- **Seafloor spreading** (Hess 1962): mid-ocean ridges are youngest; ages increase away from ridge. Vine-Matthews-Morley confirmed via magnetic anomaly stripes (symmetric about ridges + matching paleomagnetic reversals).
- **Earthquake + volcano belts**: concentrated at plate boundaries (Pacific Ring of Fire, etc.).
- **GPS measurements**: ~2-15 cm/year plate motions directly measured today.

**Major plates** (~15):
- **Pacific**: largest, mostly oceanic.
- **North American, South American, African, Eurasian, Australian, Antarctic**.
- **Indian** (sometimes combined with Australian).
- **Nazca, Cocos, Caribbean, Arabian, Philippine, Juan de Fuca, Scotia**: smaller.

**Plate speeds**: 1-15 cm/year. Pacific fastest (~10 cm/yr); African slowest (~2 cm/yr). Comparable to fingernail growth.

**Plate boundaries** (three types):
- **Divergent**: plates moving apart. Mid-ocean ridges (Mid-Atlantic, East Pacific Rise); continental rifts (East African, Rio Grande).
- **Convergent**: plates colliding. Subduction (ocean-continent: Andes; ocean-ocean: Mariana; continent-continent: Himalaya).
- **Transform**: plates sliding past horizontally. San Andreas (California), North Anatolian (Turkey), Alpine (NZ).

**Geologic features** at each:
- Divergent: rift valleys, mid-ocean ridges, basalt volcanism, shallow earthquakes.
- Convergent: trenches, volcanic arcs (subduction), folded mountains (continent-continent), deep earthquakes (down dipping slab to 700 km).
- Transform: strike-slip faults, shallow earthquakes, no volcanism (typically).

slides.title: Plate-boundary processes + Wadati-Benioff zones
slides.body:
**Subduction zones** (the most dynamic boundary):

- Denser oceanic crust subducts under continental (or another oceanic) plate.
- Earthquake hypocenters delineate the subducted slab (Wadati-Benioff zone) — slope down ~30-45°.
- Shallow events near trench; deep events 100-700 km along slab.
- Earthquakes deeper than ~700 km don't occur (mineral phase transitions + warming dissolve slab seismicity).
- Magmatism: water released from subducting slab fluxes mantle wedge → partial melting → arc volcanism 100-200 km above slab.
- Examples: Andes, Cascades, Aleutians, Japan, Indonesia.

**Megathrust earthquakes**: largest on Earth, at the contact between subducting + overriding plates.
- Magnitude 9+ possible (Cascadia, Chile, Sumatra, Tohoku).
- 2004 Indian Ocean (M9.1): >230K dead via tsunami.
- 2011 Tohoku (M9.0): tsunami + Fukushima nuclear accident.
- Recurrence: 200-600 years typical for biggest events.
- Cascadia (Pacific NW USA): last great event January 1700; statistically overdue.

**Continent-continent collision** (Himalaya):
- India crashing into Asia at ~5 cm/yr since ~50 Ma.
- Himalaya rising ~5 mm/yr; eroding at similar rate.
- Tibet thickened to ~70 km crust (vs ~35 km typical).
- Tibetan Plateau extends to drive monsoon weather; affects climate globally.

**Ocean-ocean** (Mariana Trench):
- Deepest part of ocean (~11 km).
- Older + denser plate subducts under younger.
- Volcanic island arcs above slab (Mariana Islands).

**Hotspots** (intraplate volcanism):
- Stationary mantle plumes (debated mechanism); plates move over them.
- Chain of volcanoes recording plate motion: Hawaiian-Emperor seamount chain shows Pacific plate's path over Hawaiian hotspot.
- Yellowstone, Iceland (also at MOR), Réunion, Galapagos.
- Vast eruptions (Deccan Traps, Siberian Traps) tied to mass extinctions.

**Transform faults**:
- San Andreas (California): Pacific moves NW relative to North America ~5 cm/yr.
- Strike-slip; mostly horizontal motion.
- Locked patches accumulate strain → released as earthquakes.
- 1906 San Francisco M7.9; 1989 Loma Prieta M6.9; 1994 Northridge M6.7 (separate fault).
- North Anatolian (Turkey): similar to San Andreas; 1999 Izmit M7.6, 2023 M7.8 doublet.

slides.title: Mantle convection + the deep Earth
slides.body:
**Earth's interior** (from seismology):
- **Crust**: 5-70 km. Oceanic (basalt ~7 km) + continental (granite ~35 km, up to 70 km under mountains).
- **Mantle**: 35 km - 2900 km. Solid silicate (peridotite). Ductile on geological timescales.
  - **Upper mantle** (35-660 km): includes asthenosphere (low-velocity zone, partial melt).
  - **Transition zone** (410-660 km): mineral phase changes (olivine → wadsleyite → ringwoodite → bridgmanite).
  - **Lower mantle** (660-2900 km): bridgmanite + ferropericlase.
- **Outer core** (2900-5150 km): liquid iron + nickel. Generates magnetic field (geodynamo).
- **Inner core** (5150-6371 km): solid iron + nickel. Growing as Earth cools.

**Seismic discontinuities** (sharp velocity changes):
- **Mohorovičić (Moho)**: crust-mantle boundary.
- **410 km, 660 km**: mantle phase changes.
- **Gutenberg**: mantle-outer core boundary (S-waves stop here; outer core is liquid).
- **Lehmann**: outer core-inner core boundary.

**Mantle convection**: heat from radioactive decay + core drives slow convection (~cm/yr).
- **Upwelling**: mid-ocean ridges, plume hotspots.
- **Downwelling**: subduction zones.
- Slab pull thought to drive ~70% of plate motion; ridge push ~20%.
- Whole-mantle vs layered convection — long debate; current evidence supports whole-mantle convection with some layering.

**Geodynamo**: outer-core liquid iron flow generates Earth's magnetic field. Magnetic-field reversals every ~200,000-1M years (irregular). Recorded in seafloor as alternating magnetic stripes (key plate-tectonic evidence).

**Wilson cycle**: ocean basins open + close cyclically over ~500 Myr.
1. Continental rifting (East Africa today).
2. Embryonic ocean (Red Sea today).
3. Mature ocean (Atlantic today; growing).
4. Subduction begins (Pacific today; closing).
5. Continental collision (Himalaya today).
6. Mountain decay + dispersal.

**Modern frontiers**:
- **Seismic tomography**: 3D images of mantle structure. Reveals deep slabs sinking into lower mantle + plumes rising.
- **GPS geodesy**: plate motions to mm/yr precision; intra-plate deformation; interseismic strain accumulation.
- **InSAR**: satellite radar interferometry detects surface deformation (mm-cm) from earthquakes, volcanoes, subsidence.
- **Mantle plumes vs slab dynamics**: ongoing debate about mechanisms.
- **Plate tectonics on other planets**: Earth is unique among rocky planets; Mars + Venus lack active plate tectonics.

Plate tectonics is the unifying theory: explains earthquakes, volcanism, mountain building, ocean basins, paleoclimate, even biology + evolution patterns.

question.question: Compute plate motion + the Pacific over Hawaii
question.goal: Hawaiian hotspot has produced a chain of seamounts. Distance from Kilauea to oldest Hawaiian volcano (Meiji seamount): ~5800 km. Meiji age ~85 Ma.

steps.reveal: ~6.8 cm/yr. Pacific plate moves ~7 cm/yr NW over the hotspot. Confirmed by GPS today.

steps.prompt: The Emperor seamount chain (older part) bends ~120° at ~43 Ma. What does this imply?

options: Pacific plate changed direction ~43 Ma. Before: more northerly motion. After: more NW motion. Possibly due to India-Asia collision changing global plate dynamics.

steps.reveal: Pacific plate changed direction ~43 Ma. Hotspot is approximately stationary (in deep mantle); chain bends as plate's motion shifts. Cause likely tied to India-Asia collision changing global plate-driving forces.

steps.prompt: If GPS measures 5 cm/year between Pacific + North American plates, how long until San Francisco (on N. America) + Los Angeles (on Pacific) are adjacent (currently 600 km apart)?
steps.reveal: ~12 million years. The San Andreas-style transform motion eventually brings LA to SF's latitude. Geological timescales boggle the human mind.

question.finalResult: $$\boxed{\text{Plate speed} = \text{distance}/\text{age}; \text{ Pacific} \sim 7 \text{ cm/yr; deep time matters}}$$ Plate tectonics works on million-year timescales. Hotspot tracks calibrate plate motion. GPS measures real-time motion. Combined: rigorous picture of Earth's surface evolution over deep time. India is moving north into Asia at ~5 cm/yr; in 50 Myr Indian Ocean may close further. The Pacific is shrinking; the Atlantic is growing. Geology is dynamic.

question.question: What's the evidence that confirmed seafloor spreading (Hess 1962)?
options: Vine-Matthews-Morley (1963): magnetic anomaly stripes on seafloor are SYMMETRIC about mid-ocean ridges + match the pattern of paleomagnetic reversals in time. Implies: new oceanic crust forms at ridges, records the field direction when it cools, spreads outward symmetrically.
question.explanation:
Vine-Matthews-Morley hypothesis (1963): magnetic anomaly stripes on the seafloor are SYMMETRIC about mid-ocean ridges + match the temporal pattern of paleomagnetic reversals.

Mechanism: at MOR, new basalt forms + cools, locking in Earth's current field direction. As plates spread, this strip of constant-direction basalt moves outward. New basalt records THE NEXT direction (after a reversal). Result: symmetric stripes of alternating magnetic polarity, with widths matching the known reversal chronology.

When oceanographic surveys (1960s) revealed exactly this pattern — magnetic stripes symmetric about ridges, ages increasing outward — Hess's seafloor spreading was confirmed. Combined with paleomagnetic continental-drift evidence + earthquake belt mapping → plate tectonics revolution 1965-1968.

MODERN: bathymetric + magnetic surveys + paleomagnetism + GPS all confirm. Plate tectonics now one of the most-tested + secure theories in science.

slides.workedSolution: VMM 1963: seafloor magnetic stripes symmetric about MOR + match paleomagnetic reversal chronology in time. Confirms new crust forms + spreads outward. Combined with other evidence (paleomagnetism, fossil distribution, earthquake belts) clinched plate-tectonic revolution 1965-68. Now one of science's most-tested + most-secure theories.

question.prompt: If San Andreas keeps slipping at 5 cm/yr + the seismic gap from 1857 ('Fort Tejon' M7.9) accumulates strain, walk through expected earthquake hazard.
Explain in two or three sentences why plate tectonics is described as 'the unifying theory of geology'.
question.rubric: Mentions that it explains earthquakes (at plate boundaries), volcanism (subduction + ridge + hotspots), mountain building (collisions), ocean basins (spreading + closing), paleoclimate (continental positions), even biological evolution (continental drift connecting + separating species). Single framework + decades of evidence (paleomagnetism, GPS, seismology) converging. Like Darwin for biology + atomic theory for chemistry — plate tectonics is the central organizing idea.
